flags.status: per link unit and per function: the options are a property of the source hypothesis
notes: -mno-save-restore-tocbase is inert in this fork: the variable it sets is written once in the backend and never read.  Measured: the byte-exact functions reproduce the retail bytes with the option, without it and with it added.

-mminimal-toc is what changes the code: it makes the module's TOC hold one entry per procedure instead of one entry per global, and it changes the size of the frame.  The retail's files use it or not, so the options are a property of the file.

the retail's compiler lets the register allocator choose the register that holds the link register; the reconstruction hard-codes r0 in four places of its backend.  The option -mps3-lr-reg=N reproduces the choice; see COMPILER.md and patches/.
the retail aligns its functions on four bytes and not eight, so -falign-functions=4 belongs to any byte-for-byte comparison.
-mno-toc and -mminimal-toc are not interchangeable: the first leaves the function without a frame and turns a tail call into a branch, the second decides between a clrldi and a rldicl.
